messages:
alex.chang: quick question — if we move from fixed-time windows to a hybrid admission (per-tenant soft-window + global continuous coalescer), how do we reason about SLO regressions for p99 tail?
sophie.khan: good call. main worry is headroom signalling mismatch — tenants with bursty short requests could keep getting batched into long-running coalesces and push others out of the fast-path.
diego_r: can we avoid that by separating two queues: 'fast-lane' for short sequences with stricter deadline hints and 'coalesce-lane' for longer ones? admission decides route based on seq_len_est and deadline_hint.
alex.chang: that's similar to lanes but i want to keep single runtime operator if possible. switching lanes adds scheduling complexity and cross-lane eviction protocols. any ideas for keeping single-operator semantics?
priya.s: what if admission tags requests with "deadline-class" and the continuous coalescer uses a priority-aware flush threshold: if a fast-class request arrives, it lowers the max-delay for the current batch (preemptive flush). no full eviction, just deadline-skewed flush.
sophie.khan: preemptive flush is interesting. two concerns: (1) it increases variance for long requests awaiting coalescing and (2) it may increase kernel launch overhead if we flush too often. need knob to cap preemptive flush frequency.
diego_r: metrics we should track for the experiment: batch_size_distribution by deadline-class, kernel_invocations_per_min, p50/p95/p99 latency per-class, and tenant_fairness_ratio (tokens_served_per_tenant / expectation).
alex.chang: agree. also add tail_lift_count — times a fast request forced a flush causing a long one to finish substantially later.
priya.s: implementation sketch: admission layer emits tag: {class: fast|normal|bulk, deadline_ns}. coalescer keeps two counters: oldest_deadline_in_batch and accumulated_tokens. flush_policy: if accumulated_tokens >= cap || oldest_deadline_in_batch < now + min_headroom[class] || preempt_count[class] > rate_limit then flush.
sophie.khan: sounds doable. can we avoid global locks for oldest_deadline_in_batch read? maybe use atomic snapshot and approximate counters to keep throughput.
alex.chang: yeah use per-worker ring buffers + periodic aggregator for metrics and a compare-exchange to decide flush. avoid contended global write on each admission.
diego_r: runbook for experiment: enable feature gate, route 5% prod traffic, synthetic workload with mixed short/long tails, collect metrics for 24h, rollback on >5% p99 regressions or >10% infra CPU increase.
priya.s: one more thing — we should test with KV-cache warm vs cold. batching behavior changes a lot when KV cache hits reduce decode time. add separate cohorts.
sophie.khan: +1. will draft RFC follow-up with config knobs, expected metrics, and API backwards compatibility notes (the tag is opaque to model runner).
alex.chang: thanks team. i'll spin up the canary config and add the metric dashboard. ping me if you want access to the test channel. :thumbsup:
runtime-bot: deploy-batcher-experiment gate enabled for 5% of traffic at 1764208050 (canary-id: cb-exp-12)"
